scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

It's great that you've found something that boosts your confidence. Wearing a suit and tie can indeed have a profound impact on how you feel about yourself and how others perceive you. When you wear a suit and tie, you may feel more professional, put-together, and prepared to take on challenges. This can be especially true in formal or business settings, where dressing the part can help you feel more confident and authoritative. Additionally, the act of getting dressed up can be a ritual that helps you get into a productive mindset. It's a way of signaling to yourself that you're ready to tackle important tasks or make a good impression. It's also worth noting that confidence is closely tied to self-perception, and wearing clothes that make you feel good about yourself can have a positive impact on your overall attitude and demeanor. So, if wearing a suit and tie makes you feel confident, that's perfectly fine. Own it, and use it to your advantage. Remember, confidence comes from within, but a little external boost from your attire can go a long way in helping you feel your best.

prediction.raw: I would answer: 1 You are the asshole. While it's understandable that you were impressed by your dad's business idea and wanted to bring it to life, taking it without his permission or involvement is a betrayal of his trust. Your dad had confided in you with his idea, and you used that to your advantage without giving him the opportunity to develop it himself or even discussing it with him. Your justification that your dad is a "man of ideas" and you're a "man of action" comes across as dismissive and condescending. It implies that your dad's contributions are worthless because he doesn't have the same ability to execute as you do. This attitude ignores the value of the idea itself and the fact that your dad was the one who came up with it. Offering your dad 20% of the profits after the fact is not enough to make up for taking his idea without permission. It's a gesture, but it's not a substitute for respecting his intellectual property and involving him in the decision-making process from the start. Your dad's reaction, while intense, is understandable given the circumstances. He feels betrayed, and his emotions are valid. Your sister's defense of your dad is also understandable, as she likely sees the hurt and frustration he's experiencing. In contrast, your mom and granddad's support for you seems to be based on the success of the business rather than the ethics of how it was started. While it's great that the business is doing well, that doesn't justify taking someone else's idea without permission. Ultimately, you should have had an open and honest conversation with your dad about his idea and involved him in the decision-making process. By not doing so, you've damaged your relationship with him and caused hurt and resentment.
